rv.q: What the show lacks in originality it makes up for in sheer expressiveness, though staging it in a really intimate venue would allow it to be more thrillingly in-yer-face.

'Murder Ballad' is a weak musical, even with its musical-meta mentions of famous plot clichés and a bizarre final song that was not the clever knowing wink it aimed to be, but you needn't run scared of this production: as performances go, they killed it.
Murder Ballad had everything you could ask for from a new musical, and the fact that it has a cast of Musical Theatre royalty, there really is no reason not to go.

cn.t: A slick rock musical with a thrilling score and superb cast that elevates a predictable, slight love triangle story lacking the excitement its premise promises.
